title: A dead writer whose pid was reused by an unrelated live process keeps its join-rules lock: still `locked` until a human deletes it
evidence: No start identifier is obtainable on Windows without shelling out (wmic/powershell per lock contention), so the liveness proof is pid-existence only. A reused pid reads as alive -> no takeover. Fails SAFE (availability, not mutual exclusion).
fix_direction: Record a process start identifier in the lock (Linux /proc/<pid>/stat starttime; Windows needs a native/cheap source) and treat a different start id as death. Only worth it if reuse is observed in practice.
reproduction: Write a lock {token,pid:<pid of any live process>,host:<this host>}, then recordTenantOptOut -> locked (covered by the 'pid reused by a live process' case).

title: Locks from another host, locks without a host field (written before this unit) and unparseable locks are never recovered automatically
evidence: Liveness can only be proven for a pid on this machine. A state dir shared between hosts, a legacy lock {token,pid,at}, or garbage content keeps the stale `locked` + manual-delete message. Deliberate: preferring `locked` is the safe side.
fix_direction: Operator runbook / alert on repeated `locked`; for multi-host sharing a lease with a heartbeat would be needed (not designed here).
reproduction: Existing test 'stale lock is reported ... never stolen' (legacy lock, pid 999999, no host).

title: Two check-then-act gaps remain that only matter if the liveness probe lies about a LIVE holder: ownership check -> data rename, and release rename -> restore
area: join-rules-store.ts writeAtomic owns(); join-rules-store-lock.ts releaseLock / takeOver step 4
evidence: The token re-check happens immediately before renaming the data file; a takeover landing in that microsecond window (only possible after a wrongly-judged-dead holder) is not detected. A foreign lock grabbed by release/takeover step 4 is restored with a no-replace link, but a third party creating the lock in that gap would make the restore fail.
fix_direction: None needed while pid-existence is trusted; a lease/fencing token written into the data file would close it.
reproduction: Not reproducible without injecting a lying probe plus a precisely timed second actor.

status: fixed-verified (cycle 1) except the operator-delete branch, tracked as ISS-LOCKTAKE-007
title: Takeover tombstone is a HARD LINK, so its mtime is the dead lock's own age: any contender treats another taker's live claim as abandoned and unlinks it; a slow taker then renames a LIVE new lock away, and the restore gap yields two holders and a write without the lock
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/join-rules-store-lock.ts takeOver (EEXIST branch of link, step 3 rename, step 4 restore)
evidence: 1) Real NTFS: lock backdated 1 h, fs.link to <lock>.stale.tok, stat(tomb).mtime age = 3600.017 s (same inode). So `now()-statSync(tomb).mtimeMs > max(staleMs,1000)` is true for every dead lock older than staleMs, i.e. the normal case. 2) Deterministic harness (scratchpad h/, worker-thread actors over a virtual fs running the module's real code, every fs call a scheduling point). Directed plan, 3 contenders A,B,C on a dead lock aged 100 s: A links tomb+verifies; B sees EEXIST, reclaims A's tomb, relinks its own, verifies, pauses before rename; A renames, drops tomb, creates its new lock, passes owns(); B renames A's LIVE lock to .gone, reads it, != raw; C wx-creates a lock in the gap; A writes data and releases; B's link-back fails EEXIST. Result: V1 two-believers, V2 write-without-lock, V1b write while two believers. 3) Random bursty scheduling, 3 takers, lock aged 100 s, 12000 orderings: two-believers 35, write-without-lock 27, orphan lock left 124; with the lock NOT older than staleMs, 25000 orderings: none. 4) Operator deleting the dead lock mid-takeover (4 actors, 12000 orderings): write-without-lock 62, orphan 255.
fix_direction: Make the claim a real mutex with its OWN clock: create the claim with wx as a separate file (not a link) holding its creation time, reclaim only when THAT is older than staleMs. Do not move a lock that may be live: avoid rename-then-check-then-link-back (a live lock must never be absent); if an atomic conditional removal is unavailable, serialise every acquirer behind the claim (acquirers also wx-create the claim before wx-creating the lock, or write the new lock by rename-over of the exact dead inode). Add the age>staleMs conjunct. Regress with an N>=3 interleaving test over a lock aged beyond staleMs.
reproduction: node scratchpad/h/build.mjs <lock.ts> lock.mjs; PLAN=0x4,1x4,0x3,1x3,1x7,0x5,0x3,0x2,1x1,2x3 node main.mjs lock.mjs S2 plan 1 -> V1/V2/V1b; node main.mjs lock.mjs S2 burst 12000 3 -> V1 35 runs
verified_by: checker cycle 1: claim mtime is its own (lock 3600.1 s old, claim -0.000 s); directed plan 3 takers x paused at 0..30 own steps x 200 seeds = 18600 orderings, 0 violating; random 3 takers aged 100 s 100000 orderings + 3 takers+late acquirer+2nd tenant 100000 orderings, 0 violating (old code 35/12000); young-lock control 25000 orderings, 0

title: A LIVE holder is taken over whenever kill(pid,0) cannot see it (shared lock dir across PID namespaces with equal hostname, WSL vs Windows, probe lie): silent lost update; owns() narrows but does not close it, and the no-age deviation leaves nothing else in the way
area: join-rules-store-lock.ts acquireLock deadHere; join-rules-store.ts writeAtomic owns()
evidence: Harness S4 (holder alive but probe says dead, 1 taker, 20000 random orderings): write-without-lock in 868 (4.3%): holder passes owns(), taker renames the lock, holder renames its data over the file. S5 (2 takers): two-believers 242, writes-without-lock 1369. Repo state: docker-compose sets no hostname/network_mode/pid, so containers get distinct hostnames (rule b refuses, safe) and nothing today shares a lock dir across namespaces; the api-host manifest discusses a container bind-mounting the host's raw/webinars while the scheduler runs on the Windows host (different hostnames: safe). WSL2 by default reports the Windows computer name as its hostname, a plausible path to equal hostnames with separate pid spaces. A critical section is milliseconds, so requiring lock age > staleMs (30 s) removes every one of these takeovers except a holder stalled for 30 s; the maker's argument that age adds no safety is wrong for exactly this class.
fix_direction: Require lock age > staleMs as an additional conjunct (age from the lock's own `at`/mtime; strictly fewer takeovers, so it cannot add a wrong one) and record the single-PID-namespace precondition in the contract (done) and the host's startup checks.
reproduction: harness: node main.mjs lock.mjs S4 rand 20000 7 -> V2 868 runs

Maker 10791/20000 is consistent. Age rule verified as the mitigation; honest-probe stalled holder (alive, 100 s old): 0/100000. Contract P1 strengthened accordingly.

title: A holder that dies between creating the lock (wx) and writing its content leaves an empty lock that is never recovered (strict parse fails), and the stale message tells the operator to delete by hand
area: join-rules-store-lock.ts acquireLock create (openSync wx then writeSync)
evidence: Fails safe: empty or truncated JSON never parses (a truncated object is not valid JSON, so a partial write cannot yield a truncated pid). Window is one syscall wide.
fix_direction: Treat unparseable content older than staleMs AND whose mtime is older than staleMs as abandoned only with the claim mutex from ISS-LOCKTAKE-004, or leave to the runbook.
reproduction: vfs: seed lock content '' -> never taken over

title: Takeover replaces the lock by an unconditional rename: an operator deleting the dead lock by hand inside the one-syscall gap between the re-read and the rename, with a third process creating a new lock there, loses that new lock (two holders)
evidence: Explorer residual run (3 takers + an operator delete scheduled at any step boundary, seed 20261018 series): 1938/12000 orderings violate; in reality the delete must fall inside a single syscall gap. Plain rename-over cannot be conditional on identity; alternatives (unlink then create, rename away and check) reintroduce a gap or move a live lock.
fix_direction: Document precondition P4 (never delete a lock by hand while a claim for it exists); a real fix needs fencing (a monotonic token in the data file) or an OS conditional replace.
reproduction: node --test --import tsx src/calendar/join-rules-store-lock-explore.test.ts (test 'operator deleting the dead lock inside the reread->replace gap')
rerated_by: checker cycle 1: reproduced on a real directory (taker paused before replace, hand deletion, second process acquires, taker finishes: Y owns=false, X owns=true). Needs a manual deletion inside a one-syscall gap while a takeover is in flight AND a third process creating a lock there; save-time owns() makes the displaced holder refuse its write (own explorer, operator deletes only the dead lock, 100000 orderings: live lock destroyed 1673 = 1.7%, acknowledged write lost 58 = 0.06%, new holder release unlinking the taker lock 58). Re-stat before rename would narrow but not close the gap; documented rule instead: never delete a lock by hand while any writer may run (P4). Non-blocking suggestion: add the same rule to the stale `locked` message (it says only delete the file by hand).

title: A takeover claim is left behind by a NON-crash failure (claim write fails after the exclusive create, or the claim unlink in drop() fails): takeover of that dead lock is blocked until a human removes the claim
area: join-rules-store-lock-steps.ts realFs.create (open wx, then write) and takeoverSteps create/drop
evidence: realFs.create opens `<lock>.claim.<T>` with wx and then writes; if the write throws (ENOSPC/EDQUOT/EIO) the empty file stays, the catch returns busy WITHOUT removing it, and every later taker gets EEXIST for T (verified: next healthy taker `locked`, message names the claim). drop() swallows unlink errors (one attempt), so a Windows handle without FILE_SHARE_DELETE on our fresh claim after a failed rename (EPERM measured when the lock is open elsewhere) would leave the same permanent claim. A normal acquire still works once the lock file is gone (verified). Fail-safe, availability only.
fix_direction: On a create error after the exclusive open, unlink our own partial claim; retry the unlink in drop() a few times (2-8 ms apart, bounded). Optional.
reproduction: node --import tsx chk1locktake/iss8.ts (injected ENOSPC after open): files [t.lock, t.lock.claim.deadtok1], second taker -> locked
